newsitem.title: INDIA: India, Naga separatists declare ceasefire, talks.
newsitem.headline: India, Naga separatists declare ceasefire, talks.

text.p: The Indian government and a tribal separatist group in the northeastern state of Nagaland have agreed on a ceasefire and peace talks, Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said on Friday.

"In talks with the Issac-Muivah group of the National Socialist Council of Nagaland (NSCN), it has now been agreed to a ceasefire for three months with effect from August 1, 1997, and initiate discussion at political levels," Gujral said in a statement made in parliament.
NSCN is a leading Naga tribal separatist group in a decades-old fight for an independent homeland. The hilly state near the Burmese border has a population of 1.2 million.
Gujral said the government was also in touch with other Naga separatist groups which he said had agreed to suspend insurgent activities.

Tribal activists told Reuters in Kohima, the state capital, that leaders of the Naga National Council and the NSCN (Khaplang faction) were scheduled to hold informal talks during a conference in Atlanta in the United States from July 28.
The Atlanta talks, in which Indian leaders were expected to participate, have been brokered by church leaders of the state which has a huge Christian population.

The Press Trust of India quoted a leader of NSCN (Isak-Muivah faction) as saying that the group had "decided to ceasefire for three months with effect from August 1, 1997 and begin political discussion".
